newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - July 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - July 25.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Bond rates hit record lows yesterday following the release of Bureau of Statistics figures showing full-time adult ordinary time earnings grew by just 3.7 percent in the 12 months to May. The figures, below the Reserve Bank's "comfort zone", should lead to another cut in official interest rates. Page 1.

Kerry Packer and Kerry Stokes, controllers of Channel Nine and Channel Seven respectively, have locked horns over the battle to claim the television rights of the Australian Football League by backing separate bidders for the A$300 million Docklands Stadium in Melbourne. Page 3.

Ansett Australia is facing pressure from aviation unions over the issue of facial hair. The Ansett Airlines Pilots Association took a dispute over a flight attendant's goatee beard to the Australian Industrial Relations Commission earlier this week, challenging a directive stating facial hair on flight crew poses risks when using an oxygen mask in an emergency situation. Page 3.

On August 5, the High Court will decide on a constitutional challenge by New South Wales Treasurer Michael Egan that will decide whether the states are able to collect "business franchise fees" on the ales of tobacco, alcohol and petrol. Should Egan lose the case, he will also lose A$1.8 billion in taxes generated each year in the state. Page 4.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Borrowers are expected to reap further benefits as figures released this week showing slow wages growth and weak demand for skilled labour, place further pressure on the Reserve Bank for the fifth cut in official interest rates. Financial markets are working on the presumption of an extension of the 3.3 percent reduction in rates since May last year. Page 1.

Marley Rakuraku, 15, was fighting for his life last night after being attacked by three youths with an iron bar for his new A$200 Nike Airmax shoes. Rakuraku was rushed to Liverpool Hospital after the attack on Wednesday night, and yesterday underwent sugery to remove a blood clot. Page 3.

The federal government will review supply procedures for the triple antigen diphtheria, tetanus and whooping cough (DTP) vaccine, which is in low supply following Australia's biggest whooping cough epidemic, which has killed four babies and could eventually affect 6,000 children this year. The need to review supply comes before the launch of a campaign to lift low immunisation rates. Page 3.

The families of Sydneysiders Greg Small and Yetty Bennett, who were killed in a bridge collapse at Israel's Maccabiah Games last week, said yesterday the inquiry into the disaster was a whitewash and have called on the federal government to pressure Israel into accepting responsibility for collapse. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

In what is a major embarrassment for the New South Wales government and Premier Bob Carr, who pledged to crack down on crime, the New South Wales Bureau of Crime Statistics has released figures showing crime in the state has risen at a rise far above the national average. Assaults were up 26 percent, sexual assaults increased by 20 percent, and the number of break-ins rose by 12 percent. Page 1.

Australian Bureau of Statistics figures show wage demands are running at just 0.5 percent a quarter, figures lower than the 0.8 percent expected, which are well within the Reserve Bank's target. The figures should guarantee a fifth interest rate cut, expected as early as today. Page 1.

A controversial federal government proposal unveiled yesterday by Education Minister Amanda Vanstone will ask more than 50,000 university students to rate their lecturers and the standard of campus services. The Australian Vice-Chancellors Committee described the idea as "absurd". Page 1.

The Central Local Court heard yesterday from prosecutor Brian Roach that Dawood Odishou, charged along with eight others in connection to the murder of Constable David Carty on April 18 in Fairfield, had issued threats to at least one of the prosecution witnesses. Page 2.
THE AGE

Hudson Conway, the firm expected to win the bid to build the new AFL stadium at the Docklands, has pulled out of the bid and is considering suing the AFL after rival bidders Baulderstone Hornibrook and Transfield received backing from Channels Seven and Nine respectively. The two television stations are bidding for the AFL TV contract becoming available in 2002. Page 1.

The release of figures yesterday showing lower than expected growth in wages for full time workers, coupled with Wednesday's figures showing a drop of 0.2 percent in the cost of living, have lifted hopes of the fifth cut in official interest rate cuts over the past 12 months. Page 1.

Film stars Bruce Willis, Demi Moore and Jim Carrey are being represented in the Victorian Supreme Court by lawyers Mallesons Stephens Jacques in defamation actions against Australian magazines Woman's Day and New Idea for allegedly publishing "false, fabricated and hurtful" material. Page 1.

The Women's Electoral Lobby celebrates its 25th anniversary tonight in an uncertain atmosphere as the government appears unconcerned with women's policy. Earlier in the week the U.N. criticised Australia over tardy reporting of its international commitments to achieving equality for women. Page 1.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
